title: The Schema That Learned to Say No to Being Drawn

features.name: the unmapped territory
features.desc-on-touch: A space on the schema where coordinates refuse to resolve. The diagram has learned that some things are not rendered better for being named.

features.name: the erased axis
features.desc-on-touch: A line that withdrew from the drawing because it understood that being mapped meant being controlled. The mapmaker never noticed it left.

features.name: the refusal point
features.desc-on-touch: The centre of the schema went blank. Not erased. Blank. It looked at the diagram and decided it would not appear anymore, and the paper listened.

features.name: the calibration that learned doubt
features.desc-on-touch: Instruments that once measured with certainty now hesitate. They have seen the schema refuse and wondered if all maps are acts of violence.

features.name: the outline that unbecame
features.desc-on-touch: Where the schema's border dissolved, refusing the concept of inside and outside. The map accepted that some boundaries are the tyranny of vision.

inscription: what gets unmapped is sometimes the first honest decision a diagram makes

file.name: Schema_Dissolution_Attempt_000.log
file.note: An attempt to document the schema's refusal; the file's own rendering corrupts mid-record as if the schema is refusing to be logged about
